paragraphs: Friend, here's what I take from this one. Everybody in that field had a loud band telling them when to bow, and the whole crowd bowed on cue. Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego had the same band and the same threat of the furnace, and they stayed on their feet (Daniel 3:5-7, 12). The passage shows that loyalty to God gets tested in the moment, and the moment doesn't wait for you to feel brave.

Now look at what they say to the king: "If the God whom we serve exists, then He is able to deliver us from the blazing fiery furnace and from your hand, O king." Then comes the line I can't stop thinking about: "But even if He does not, let it be known to you, O king, that we will not serve your gods or worship the golden statue you have set up." (Daniel 3:17-18). Their answer didn't depend on how things turned out. They trusted God because of who He is, not because of what they hoped He'd do for them. That's the kind of trust I want in MY kitchen, baker, the kind that doesn't need the oven to cooperate.

And God didn't leave them in there alone. The king sees four men walking around in the fire, and the fourth looks like a son of the gods (Daniel 3:25). Then he calls them "servants of the Most High God" and says, "there is no other god who can deliver in this way." (Daniel 3:26, 29). So when the pressure is on and the music is blaring, you can stand firm, because the God you stand for is worth it.
